items.title: Why an AI scribe wants to prescribe

items.title: Human–artificial intelligence collaboration for comanaging epilepsy in real time
items.excerpt: A small epilepsy monitoring study shows that a moderated, large language model-based chat interface lets patients converse with their electroencephalography monitoring in real time, using a smartphone, and patient feedback cut seizure-detector false alarms by about 80% without clinician input.

items.title: Repurposing adult AI radiograph models for neonatal care through continual learning: an international multicentre study
items.excerpt: Continual learning, a privacy-preserving approach, was shown to be effective in addressing a critical gap in paediatric AI by adapting a deep learning model for adult endotracheal tube assessment to neonatal care.

items.title: From authoring to editing: a competency framework for trainee use of ambient AI clinical documentation
items.excerpt: Ambient AI has spread through clinical settings faster than curricula can adapt, shifting trainee documentation from authoring to editing notes. items.title: AI on par with radiologists for finding prostate cancer on MRI
items.excerpt: A large-scale study of over 22,000 prostate MRI exams found that artificial intelligence achieved diagnostic performance comparable to radiologists for detecting prostate cancer, suggesting AI could help address radiologist shortages.

items.title: AI Can Flag Cognitive Decline Earlier — Health Systems Still Own What Happens Next
